irac.issue: Whether the income from an impartible estate is taxable as the income of the individual members of the family or as the income of the family as a whole.
irac.rule: The income from an impartible estate is taxable as the income of the individual members of the family, and not as the income of the family as a whole.
irac.application: The Supreme Court held that the income from the impartible estate of the Raja of Gobardhan is taxable as the income of the individual members of the family, and not as the income of the family as a whole. The Court also held that the previous decision in Commissioner of Income-tax v. Ram Raj Bahadur (1953) is not applicable in this case.
irac.conclusion: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal of the Commissioner of Income-tax and set aside the order of the Calcutta High Court.

authority_results.cited: Commissioner of Income-tax v. Ram Raj Bahadur (1953) 23 ITR 553
